⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ 10/10 – One of the most unique indie games I've played

Cult of the Lamb perfectly blends roguelike combat, base management, and dark humor into something that feels fresh from start to finish. Building and managing your cult is surprisingly addictive, and there's always something to do, whether it's recruiting followers, upgrading your settlement, or venturing into dungeons to take down bosses.

The art style is amazing—cute on the surface but with a dark, twisted charm that gives the game its personality. The soundtrack fits perfectly, and the gameplay loop keeps you coming back for "just one more run."

The developers have also continued supporting the game with updates, adding even more content and quality-of-life improvements over time.

If you enjoy roguelikes, management games, or just want something different, Cult of the Lamb is absolutely worth playing.

Pros:

Fun and addictive gameplay loop
Great art style and animations
Engaging cult management mechanics
Excellent soundtrack
Regular updates and new content

Cons:

Some late-game tasks can feel repetitive

Overall, Cult of the Lamb is a fantastic indie game that balances charm, humor, and challenging gameplay exceptionally well. Highly recommended. 🐑👑

citations.review_text: i love this game, when i see my followers turn against me, it makes me blast my bashful boy load in their faces to get them back in their place. i love walking out of the tent to smell the musk of daddies furry kittens laying on the floor for me like good boys. got me really violating the geneva convention with how much excrement be layin on the floor from my time away crusading. 10/10

You sure do unlock a lot of stuff in this game. And cross a lot of things off a lot of lists. The roguelike elements are simple and engaging enough to keep you occupied for a while. The "cozy" elements will have you constantly running around cleaning ♥♥♥♥, vomit, corpses and broken down buildings in a way that won't let you rest or relax. Still, this is a fun and gripping title if you're into this type of gameplay. Personally, I am into this kind of gameplay for about 15 hours and then I get the feeling I've unlocked enough decorations and outfits.

Part of me wants to heed the saying, "if you don't have anything nice to say, don't say anything at all," but this game is mean and brutal, so here I am!  Lol

I really wanted to like this game.  It really is fun and the systems are interesting, varied, and mostly well-done.  But the fact remains, I got frustrated the longer I played.

Eventually you just always feel like you're losing progress or behind on something.  Cultists are aging and dying, base is getting run down, tasks getting behind (preaching, talking, fishing, cleaning), village losing faith and hunger and health....it eventually felt more like a chore and I stopped wanting to play.

I do love how much the game offers and I personally enjoyed the combat runs and controls on Steam Deck.  I guess it just isn't the chill, relaxing, calm, sacrificing-villager type game I was looking for.

PROS

+ Lots of systems to manage your personal cult
+ Ability to customize every villager
+ Many different skills, weapons, items, and collectibles
+ Fun developing your cult's ideology, research, and buildings

CONS

- Time is ALWAYS against you (turn off time progression during combat runs ASAP!)
- Villagers die off way too quickly
- Combat aiming and controls are pretty clunky
- Can feel overwhelming if you don't stay on top of everything

Would play this game a lot on the switch and that's why I bought it on Steam because this game is very fun. If you love fighting, customizing and getting attached to NPCs then this is for you. This game is smooth with movement and different difficulties when starting. It can either be a cozy kinda game with just a bit of fighting to progress or can be upgrading and trying you're best at keeping everyone happy, or even just trying to defeat different bosses. Overall, this game is not hard unless you make it.

Getting to name your followers of your cult is the best thing. It will play with emotions if you get attached easily. You can even have an option to marry your own followers and each follower even has their own personality. Your goal is to keep your cult alive while your followers are also dying left and right. You give them tasks around the cult like collect resources, growing plants for food, cooking, etc. You can also give them special necklaces either to make them worker harder, to never sleep, become immortal, to live twice as long, to move faster, a chance to harvest bonus resources, etc. AND even some followers can rebel against you so make sure to watch out.

And don't even get me started on the soundtrack. 
Soundtrack is a 10/10.

This game is super good and full of content that I can't even fit in this review.

[u][b] BACKGROUND: [/b][/u]

Listen... at the time of this review, I have yet to finish this game. I have yet to kill the big bad... and yet, I felt the uncontrollable urge to leave this review (Just brainwashed cult things I guess).

[u][b] APPEALS: [/b][/u]

While the gameplay aspect of this game isn't new to those of us used to playing dungeon crawler-esque games, Cult of the Lamb (COTL) brings a unique world-building and narrative experience to the genre. Aside from the amazingly crafted dungeons, COTL also has unique non-dungeon puzzles and side quests/mini-games (why did I think I was in Stardew Valley for a moment?). Gameplay is also seamless (I haven't come across a stutter, bug or crash).

That being said, most dungeon crawlers are notoriously difficult. If you're like me (enjoying a good challenge but lost interest/energy when things become too tedious/grindy - hey! I'm a patient person, I swear), then you'll appreciate the difficulty system in COTL. There are three difficulty tiers and you can choose between them at any time. There are no achievements linked to the game difficulty.

While the game mechanics are simple and easy to understand, the game is sufficiently challenging without being suffocating or frustrating. For example, you must manage certain resources to effectively play the game. These resources are hard to acquire in the beginning but eventually it becomes a non-issue (I have yet to finish the game and I've already outgrown resource use - except food). As you progress, resource management becomes easier, and towards the end-game content, resource management is not the issue; gameplay choices and time management are. So there's a bit of healthy pressure, but the game is not tedious or grindy.

The artwork and music are well crafted. COTL is bright, colourful and incredibly adorable with the art style (unique from many games in its genre). The music is upbeat, fun, and it never gets boring even on repeat.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game runs well and is well-optimized even on older or lower-spec computer hardware.

citations.review_text:
Hello there. Since I own an old pc I figured that making a review could help others see how games (in this case, Cult of the Lamb) run on dated hardware. So that's what I'll do first. After that, i'll review the game itself.

[h1] Game Optimisation [/h1]
Settings i played on: 1080p with graphics set to high (shadows/particles on) running at around 50-60 fps (my monitor can do max 60fps). Game installed on HDD
The minimum requiremets for this game are very forgiving and easily accessible even to older pc's models. As for my experience, I didn't have any major FPS drops during normal gameplay. The game was smooth with little to no input lag. I never had any performance or driver compatibility issues. Considering my pc is from the AM3+ era (2012) i can say pretty confidently that this game is [b] WELL OPTIMIZED [/b]. I, with my specs, was above the minimum requirements (which says a lot). Based on my experience, systems close to the minimum requirements should still have a good chance of running the game by lowering the resolution and graphics settings. The Only thing worth mentioning is that an Outdated gpu driver might make the experience unstable (but that's something the game can't do much about). Long Gameplay Sessions could also cause some rare fps drops (still we are talking about a drop of max 10 fps).

9.5/10

[h1] The Game [/h1]
[h3] Graphics [/h3]
The Graphics are clean, polished and fluid for a 2d Game. The Art style is cute and the Animations are Cartoonish but not out of place. The Colours are really bright and lively which is expected with an Art Style such as that. To sum it up, they are well done and they match the game's vibe. Whether you enjoy it will mostly depend on how much you like colourful and cartoonish art styles even although, just by looking at the game's store page, it should immediately be clear to you (the trailer and photos showcase the art style/Graphics pretty well on their own)

10/10

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a combination of base management and action roguelike dungeon crawling mechanics.

citations.review_text: very fun base builder and rogue like

A game overflowing with style. The cutesy aesthetic mixed with brutal Eldritch visuals and themes was super unique and executed masterfully. The OST was iconic, and the overall art direction and sound design were superb. 

The game was split into two main halves → the cult management side and the action roguelike side. The former had seamless integration of the game’s horror elements, whether with sacrifices, doctrines, rituals, etc. It was simple, but it made up for it with polished and engaging gameplay. However, the roguelike elements were underwhelming. While the combat was polished, it felt fairly generic and lacked the thematic cohesion present in the base-building side.

If the visuals interest you, I recommend giving it a try, particularly if you like base-building games.

citations.review_text: honestly a 10/10, the story is great combat is great, characters are great and it has very good art and music design

This game was absolutely adorable and super fun to play. The music was delightful, the art and animation were unique and beautiful, and all the mechanics felt highly intuitive. The story is not that deep, but it's not the main focus of the game. I enjoyed the base building and management portion more than the rogue-lite combat in the crusades. I spent a lot of time moving things around, making my systems more efficient, and making room for everything I wanted to build.

The game is all about managing your cult, recruiting and indoctrinating followers, exploring dungeons to get rewards, beating the big bad guys, and keeping your cultists happy. You get to do many "culty" things like sacrificing followers, turning them into demons to bring them with you into dungeons, performing rituals, and brainwashing them. The contrast between the adorable art style and making your followers become cannibals or other similar things is hilarious.

I got attached to so many of my followers, only to realize they could die for several reasons. It broke my heart to see some of them go, but FRET NOT! Necromancy is also a thing here, hehe. You will unlock mechanics that allow you to keep your followers alive longer, but you'll see quite a few die before that happens.

Once you finish the game for the first time, you unlock a new entity and the 'postgame' begins. Once you finish the postgame, you can still go into the dungeons to unlock achievements and collectibles, as well as to explore and have fun.

I only got one DLC and it was purely cosmetic, most of them are. I don't think it was necessary tho; the base game comes with a lot of customization options already. They recently released a new DLC with more story and mechanics, so you'll have even more content to go through if you like the game.

I played with both a controller and the keyboard, since some things were easier to do with the K&M (like fishing or building/decorating), while fighting felt better with the controller.

citations.review_text:
[h2] I've wasted 143 hours of my life on this game. 10/10, would do again. [/h2] 

The gameplay is so repetitive, but it just never seems to get old. The devs dangle the carrot just far enough infront of your face that you always want to chase it. I'm not sure if it's the constant rewards, new scenery and lands, or just the idea of working towards eventually killing those heretic Gods that keeps you going, but it got me hooked.

[h3] The good: [/h3]
Design -  I'll admit, it took me a moment to get used to the art style but now I can see it as nothing more than peak planning. It feels like every corner you look into, the artists poured their heart and soul into the design of the creatures, wildlife, bosses, and even just your decor.

Gameplay - I enjoy the idea of brand new battle chambers to traverse with every dive into each forest. You can never guess where the next perk room is gonna be, or if you're going to wander annoyingly deep into a waste of time. It makes you plan and decide just how fast you need to get back to your cult.

Bosses - They proved a fair enough challenge, especially whilst trying to get the "No Damage" achievements, but their attack patterns were refreshingly predictable and allowed you to have enough time to dodge out of the way without making it too easy.

In short, it allows you to play the game calmly, but keeps your attention on the next move you ought to take.

[h3] The bad: [/h3]

There's not much I have to say for this section 

Building - Inevitably, you'll need to design your cult and put new structures down. Maybe it's just me, but I hated the way each structure was laid out on a diamond grid and how it didn't provide atleast a faint outline so you could plan out your cult. Other than that,  I had no issue for finding the right piece of decoration for the right spot in my cult. They really had everything you could possibly want and need - even if it makes you wonder "Why and how would anyone use that?"

This is the kind of game tha…

claims.claim: Reviewers report performance drops and stuttering specifically within the shrine and inspiration skill tree menus.

citations.review_text:
I would like to start by saying that I love this game, it is amazing. Unfortunately, every so often it freezes up my computer. I know that is probably more to do with my AMD hardware than it is with the game but I have a whole bunch of other games that play just fine on this hardware. So, as much as I would like to recommend this game I cannot due to it's unplayability. If someone reads this review and can direct me on how to make it stop freezing up I would love to change it to a positive recommendation.

EDIT: I found that if I turn V-sync off and turned down a few of my graphical settings the game will play without freezing up. This is not as good as I would like but it is fine. My drivers are automatically kept up to date so that's not the issue. I have had some issues with a desktop companion app that I keep running pretty much 24/7 so I have unfounded theories that it may have something to do with it. Since I was able to get the game running without freezing I've changed the recommendation to thumbs up instead of down. I will do more troubleshooting and see if it was indeed the desktop companion (Chippu) or not.

EDIT 2: I turned off my background programs and the game still froze up, specifically after losing to a boss on the transfer back to cult screen. 

EDIT 3: Found that the V-sync is the issue. Turned it off and the crashes stopped. So, I'll keep the recommended on the review but that is an issue that some people may get.

I've been playing this game since 2024, one of my favorite games EVER i love it, however i have just a few complaints regarding optimization, the game runs great.. just some of my pcs.. most menus and stuff are okay despite some stuttering on less powerful devices its SPECIFICALLY the shrine and inspiration skilltrees that make me want to bash my head in a wall i have no idea what kinda special 3d effect or something like that is going on in the bg but it makes the game lag so bad it takes me like 30 minutes to even select what i wanted to upgrade ive gone in situations where i would just try avoid and save up the upgrades so i could use them when playing on my better pc plz fix this add a toggle or something to turn it off. The game is crafted with a lot of love and i would absolutely recomend it to anyone
